correctness.rationale: The binary proof extends over a fixed q-ary alphabet after replacing complementary run boundaries by arbitrary symbols unequal to the edited symbol. The simple-path/shared-source, random-hash, witness, and component arguments are alphabet-independent; q-ary inserted/transfer symbols change only fixed constants. Keeping the original k=2 ceil(log_2 n)+2 also preserves the large-witness estimate.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The motivating 2026 preprint explicitly lists fixed larger alphabets and coefficient 2t-1 as open. Searches over q-ary/nonbinary multiple-deletion codes, equivalent redundancy formulations, the source identifier/title, and the SCOPE archive found no prior coverage. The source is extremely recent, so near-simultaneous or revision risk remains.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an explicit open extension in the motivating paper and lowers the classical existential leading redundancy coefficient from 2t to 2t-1 for every fixed q-ary alphabet, showing the factor-n gain is not a binary-only phenomenon.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
